mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a single month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of future earnings for equities and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same regime are not statistically lower than during pre-tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +0.5% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations that prompt the Fed to hike rates, which compresses equity discounting and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over a 6-month window, 20-day forward returns during such CPI moves are not statistically worse than during prior low-inflation periods (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS of at least 2% for two consecutive months indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-on-month increase ≥ 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Empirical power of the signal falls below 0.05 in out-of-sample tests during periods of high unemployment or weak wage growth (e.g., recession).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of HOUST exceeds 1,350 units for the first time in a month, it reflects robust industrial production momentum that raises aggregate demand, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The effect is not statistically significant in periods of simultaneous supply shocks or negative consumer sentiment (IC < 0.05, two-tailed).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (≥ 2% month-on-month) accompanied by a simultaneous rise in GDPC1 (≥ 3% month-on-month) signals a supply-side contraction that outpaces demand growth, compressing equity valuations and generating negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-on-month change ≥ -2% AND GDPC1 month-on-month change ≥ +3%
failure_condition: The interaction is not robust across multiple supply shocks (e.g., oil, semiconductor) or when demand recovers simultaneously (p-value interaction test > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months, it reflects labor market softening and reduced wage growth expectations, which lowers growth prospects and produces negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE month-on-month decline for three consecutive months below 3.5%
failure_condition: The effect is absent during periods of simultaneous monetary easing or strong job growth (e.g., unemployment falls below 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in RSAFS of at least 10% over two consecutive months suggests reduced investor liquidity in the money market, which amplifies equity market volatility and tends to precede negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS month-on-month decline ≥ -10% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The signal is not predictive in periods of high liquidity from central bank operations or emergency lending facilities (e.g., during S&L crisis).

mechanism_narrative: When the 4-week moving average of GDPC1 exceeds 24,000 (in chained 2017 dollars) while UNRATE remains below 4%, it indicates robust business activity outpacing wage growth, which supports equity valuation expansion and positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The interaction is not significant when supply constraints are binding or consumer sentiment is weak (e.g., during a tech sector downturn).
